headline: Would have canceled a federal wildlife plan for managing barred owls in Washington, Oregon, and California; the Senate did not take it up.
what_it_does: This resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act to cancel a decision by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service called the Barred Owl Management Strategy. The strategy covers how the agency manages barred owls in Washington, Oregon, and California. If adopted, the strategy would have had no legal effect. The agency also could not have issued a substantially similar rule unless Congress later allowed it.

who_it_affects.how: The agency would have lost its approved barred owl management plan for these three states and been barred from adopting a substantially similar one without new action by Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Landowners, tribes, and land managers in Washington, Oregon, and California
who_it_affects.how: Any barred owl management work planned under the strategy in their areas would not have gone forward under that plan.
